title: Constant coefficients on the pro-etale site
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a finite discrete ring (not necessarily commutative) and let $u:U\to V$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $\Lambda_{T,\Proet}$ be the sheaf of rings of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $u^{-1}$ for inverse image of sheaves of rings, left adjoint to the direct image of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For $a\in\Lambda$ write $\eta_T(a)$ for the section obtained from the constant function $a$ by the sheafification defining $\Lambda_{T,\Proet}$. Define $\rho:\Lambda_{V,\Proet}\to u_*\Lambda_{U,\Proet}$ by sending each constant section $a$ on an object $W\to V$ to $\eta_U(a)$ restricted to $W\times_VU$; on an element of the defining presheaf use these sections on its open fibres and glue, then extend uniquely by sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Let $c_u:u^{-1}\Lambda_{V,\Proet}\to\Lambda_{U,\Proet}$ be the ring-sheaf morphism adjoint to $\rho$. Then $c_u$ is an isomorphism. For commutative $\Lambda$, under the unique identifications with constant sheaves preserving constant sections, this is exactly the structure map $c^u_\Lambda$ in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Here inverse image and the coefficient objects are sheaves, with the indicated sheafifications; in particular for $U=\varnothing$ both sides are the zero ring sheaf and $c_u$ is its unique isomorphism.

proof.text: The empty family covers the empty object of any $T_{\Proet}$: the arrow condition in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] is vacuous and zero affine opens cover its only affine open, which is empty. The sheaf gluing axiom then says that every ring sheaf $G$ has exactly one section on that object: the empty matching family has a unique amalgamation. Consequently $G(\varnothing)$ is the zero ring. If $T=\varnothing$, every object mapping to $T$ is empty, so every ring sheaf on $T_{\Proet}$ is uniquely isomorphic to the zero ring sheaf. In particular both the sheafification defining $\Lambda_{T,\Proet}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] and the sheafification defining $u^{-1}\Lambda_{V,\Proet}$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] are zero ring sheaves when $U=\varnothing$; any presheaf value before sheafification does not change this conclusion [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. For any $G$ on the empty site, both $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{ShRing}}(\Lambda_{T,\Proet},G)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ring}}(\Lambda,G(T))$ are singletons. There is a unique unital ring map from any ring to the zero ring. Constant sections need not be distinct: here $\eta_T(0)=\eta_T(1)=0=1$. Thus the ring-operation and unit-preservation conditions below hold also on empty objects.

source.place: Remark Tag 04B3 (remark-sheaf-condition-empty-covering); proetale.tex Tag 09A5 (section-morphism); direct application of the sheaf gluing axiom

proof.text: Put $P_T(W)=\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|W|),\Lambda)$ as in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Pullback along the quotient $|W|\to\pi_0(|W|)$ identifies its elements with continuous functions $|W|\to\Lambda$: a continuous map to a discrete space is constant on each connected component, and the quotient topology is exactly the condition for the descended function to be continuous. For each such function $s$, its fibres $W_a=s^{-1}(a)$ are clopen subsets, not connected components. Regard them as open subschemes. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], open immersions are weakly etale and composition with $W\to T$ gives objects of $T_{\Proet}$ (use that lemma with auxiliary commutative ring $\mathbf Z$; no coefficient claim of that lemma is needed). They cover $W$ in the topology of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]: any affine open is covered by affine opens inside the fibres, and quasi-compactness gives a finite subcover. On $W_a$, $s$ is the constant $a$.

proof.text: For a sheaf of rings $G$ on $T_{\Proet}$, restriction to constant functions gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{PShRing}}(P_T,G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ring}}(\Lambda,G(T))$. Indeed a ring map $\alpha:\Lambda\to G(T)$ sends $s\in P_T(W)$ to the unique glued section whose restriction to $W_a$ is $\alpha(a)|_{W_a}$. Distinct fibres have empty intersection; a sheaf has a unique section on the empty object, so these sections agree on overlaps. On $W_a\cap W_b$ for the simultaneous fibres of $s,t$, the glued values are $\alpha(a),\alpha(b)$, so the values of $s+t$ and $st$ are $\alpha(a+b)$ and $\alpha(ab)$; uniqueness of gluing proves preservation of both operations. The constant functions $0,1$ map to $0,1$; these may coincide, as Step 1 proves on the empty object. No injectivity of the map of constants is asserted. For a morphism $W'\to W$, the fibres of the restricted function are the inverse images of $W_a$, so restriction and gluing give the same section. Conversely any natural transformation is determined by its values on constants at $T$, since $T$ is terminal and the fibre family covers. By [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] and $P_T^\#=\Lambda_{T,\Proet}$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], this gives natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{ShRing}}(\Lambda_{T,\Proet},G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ring}}(\Lambda,G(T))$, with $h$ corresponding to $a\mapsto h_T(\eta_T(a))$.

source.place: Example Tag 0H7J (example-constant-sheaf), with the ring-valued sheafification universal property, and proetale.tex Section Tag 09A5 (Functoriality of the pro-etale site); correction of the blueprint proof

proof.text: Compare this with the constant sheaf of [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]: let $C_T$ be the sheafification of the constant ring presheaf. The constant functions give $q:C_T\to P_T^\#$. Applying the gluing construction to the canonical map $\Lambda\to C_T(T)$ gives $r:P_T^\#\to C_T$. The composite $rq:C_T\to C_T$ agrees with $\mathrm{id}_{C_T}$ after precomposition with the canonical map from the constant presheaf, and hence equals $\mathrm{id}_{C_T}$ by the sheafification universal property; $qr$ is the identity on every constant function and therefore on each $s$ by its fibre cover, and hence on $P_T^\#$ by the sheafification universal property. These identifications preserve constants. This is the constant-ring-sheaf characterization of [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], proved here directly from its definition; it is not the module unit-Hom characterization.

source.place: Example Tag 0H7J (example-constant-sheaf), with the ring-valued sheafification universal property, and proetale.tex Section Tag 09A5 (Functoriality of the pro-etale site); correction of the blueprint proof

proof.text: For every ring sheaf $G$ on $U_{\Proet}$, use the ring-sheaf adjunction and direct-image evaluation of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], and Step 3 for $U,V$, to obtain natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{ShRing}(U)}(u^{-1}\Lambda_{V,\Proet},G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{ShRing}(V)}(\Lambda_{V,\Proet},u_*G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ring}}(\Lambda,(u_*G)(V))=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ring}}(\Lambda,G(U))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{ShRing}(U)}(\Lambda_{U,\Proet},G)$. Here $V\times_VU\cong U$ is the terminal base-change identification. The map $\rho$ in the statement exists by Step 3 applied to $u_*\Lambda_{U,\Proet}$ and $a\mapsto\eta_U(a)$. For $h:\Lambda_{U,\Proet}\to G$, the adjunct of $h\circ c_u$ is $u_*h\circ\rho$; at $V$ this sends $a$ to $h_U(\eta_U(a))$. Thus under the displayed bijections precomposition with $c_u$ is the identity of $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ring}}(\Lambda,G(U))$, so it is bijective. Both compared Hom functors have the same ring-sheaf category as their target category. For commutative $\Lambda$, Step 4 identifies both coefficient sheaves with the constant-presheaf sheafifications, preserving constants. Under these identifications, $\rho$ agrees on every constant section with the presheaf map specifying $c^u_\Lambda$ in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. The sheafification universal property makes the two maps to the direct image equal, and the adjunction makes their adjuncts equal. This proves the stated agreement with $c^u_\Lambda$.

source.place: Example Tag 0H7J (example-constant-sheaf), with the ring-valued sheafification universal property, and proetale.tex Section Tag 09A5 (Functoriality of the pro-etale site); correction of the blueprint proof

proof.text: Write $A=u^{-1}\Lambda_{V,\Proet}$, $B=\Lambda_{U,\Proet}$ and $c=c_u:A\to B$ in the single category $\mathrm{ShRing}(U_{\Proet})$. Surjectivity of $(-)\circ c:\operatorname{Hom}(B,A)\to\operatorname{Hom}(A,A)$ supplies $d:B\to A$ with $d\circ c=\mathrm{id}_A$. Injectivity of $(-)\circ c:\operatorname{Hom}(B,B)\to\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)$ applied to $(c\circ d)\circ c=c=\mathrm{id}_B\circ c$ gives $c\circ d=\mathrm{id}_B$. Hence $c$ is invertible, without any identification or change of module coefficient categories.
